articles.title: Ocean City Harbor - Normal - Wave Race: Blue Storm Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Wave Race: Blue Storm at IGN: walkthroughs, items, maps, video tips, and strategies
articles.body:
Ocean City Harbor is the spiritual successor to the Fortress track in Wave Race 64 . This visually stimulating night course will dazzle you with large waves, cool reflections, and plenty of floating debris. Note that the water level changes depending on your weather setting.

There's a major shortcut on this track at 1 that requires skill and concentration as you don't just have to navigate a narrow passage, but you also incur three missed buoys. It's worth it, though. You're well-advised to take it on the first or last lap. Doing it early gives you an idea of how many more misses you can still afford. There is a yellow buoy, listed below as the "outlier buoy" that's a good skip on lap 2. But if the above shortcut feels too risky, you can also just do the buoy skip three times instead.

There is also a hidden boost ramp on the Normal version of the track at location 2 , but it requires the water level to be high. That said, even then it's not the best. You'll incur a skip, losing whatever Turbo you have built up. We explain it more under the Rainy condition lower on the page as the water is high from the get-go.

There are other opportunities and challenges. Debris is everywhere, which you should always avoid. Metal containers that fall into the water can be used as ramps for jumps. While good for building Turbo via tricks, it's often faster to just go around them.

Ignore the tunnel openings you pass. On Normal, they are chained up and can't be used. But they're obviously there for a reason.

Rule #1: Do a trick whenever you boost and no other racers are directly next to you (or behind you). It'll get you valuable turbos at the right time. To start off, hit your boost right at the start and head towards the area in between the two buoys ahead. As soon as you engage the turbo, perform a simple trick to refill your turbo meter with one point.

Don't hold the trick or you risk falling off when you hit a ramp or debris floating in the water. The water level is at a high point so the first of the two ramps that follow is almost covered. You can safely hop over the first one (don't boost right in front of it -- it knocks some riders off their rides) and land in the water just before the second ramp. Jump slightly towards the right to set yourself up for the next buoy. If you're having trouble with these ramps, you can also go around them on the left, but I suggest waiting until the second lap for this as the water level will have dropped and you'll actually save time that way.

Head straight towards the left side of the yellow marker and turn hard right (while pressing R ).

Hit your turbo boost at the same time and speed towards the left side of the tanker ahead of you. Going in a straight line, pass all the buoys on your way until your turbo meter is full again. Engage your boost (careful, don't steer too much or you'll miss buoys -- you might also want to not do tricks on this stretch just to be safe), pass the tug boats and narrowly miss the submerged ramp on the right side. Hitting it will just slow you down, so don't bother.

Turn right at the yellow buoy and once again hit your turbo button to ride the waves that roll in from the left. Hit your next turbo as soon as you get it and pass the start gate.

Stick more towards the left side of the track as one of the boats has moved away from the wall to get in your way. Head towards the first two buoys, but this time, don't jump the ramps (which both stick out of the water now). Instead, follow the left wall and bypass one or both ramps. It's time to cheat a little now... Instead of following the course, head to the right before you pass the red buoy.

The area in question is to the right of the electric blue arrow signs, marked on the map with 1 . Watch out for the poles! Your safest way through is to pass the second pole from the right side and head for the gray/red wall ahead, then turn. Don't get distracted by the "Miss!" warnings that flash on screen and make a right and a left to successfully navigate the narrow passage that follows. When you come out on the other side, you will have incurred three misses, but you'll also have shaved a few seconds off your lap time! Finish the rest of the lap.

Since you can't take the shortcut twice, you'll have to race lap 3 just like lap 1, but with one major difference. The water level is now very low, so the ramps really stick out. Your best bet is to hit your turbo boost just when you're about to hit the first ramp. The added speed will propel you high into the air, clearing both ramps in one jump. Pro racers will want to pull off a fancy trick in the air to build up boost power again, but you'll do fine without it as well.

There are two ways to deal with the next yellow buoy and it all depends on how full your turbo meter is. If it's completely full or completely (or almost) empty, you should purposely skip this yellow buoy and take a narrow right turn (while boosting, if available).

You can also take this shortcut on your first lap if the conditions are right, but remember that you can only miss one buoy if you've taken the large shortcut in lap 2. When you get around the next corner, you will notice a new obstacle in your way.

A metal crate has fallen on lap 2 and is swimming in the water and will act as a ramp. Hit it or avoid it, but don't let it distract you. Finish the race by boosting as much as you can. And don't forget to do tricks while boosting.

For a different experience, take the shortcut on lap 1. You will then see the crate fall on lap 2.

The differences between sunny and partially cloudy weather on this course are merely cosmetic. Follow the instructions above.

In this case, the water level starts off low and then rises in subsequent laps.

In essence, the water depth is reversed from the previous conditions. Adjust your strategy accordingly. The waves are also slightly higher, but they shouldn't adversely affect your racing line.

The water level has dramatically changed. Remember all those pillars that you had to avoid when you previously took the lap 2 shortcut?

That's all underwater now, so you can take that same shortcut without worrying over collisions.

Although the basic course remains the same, a hidden boost ramp is now accessible in the northwestern corner of the track at 2 . But the fact that it's there doesn't mean you should take it.

As you pass the yellow buoy in the south, you can head towards the wall instead of immediately turning right. You can now use the stone ramp to jump and boost, but you will miss the red buoy on the other side, making this boost less effective than simply bypassing the previous yellow track marker in the first place. One quick note on the ramp height: despite the high water level, the two ramps close to the start remain high, which kind of throws a damper on this weather condition being perfect for quick lap times...

But you can of course always go around them or use a boost to jump them if you're having problems. Just pay attention on lap 3 as the first ramp tends to bump riders off.

More rain, lower waves. Read the above description to get an idea of what's changed over the clear weather conditions.

Even though the water level is at its highest, you won't find any new shortcuts.

articles.title: In Silksong, spite is my motivation to keep playing
articles.summary: Hollow Knight: Silksong is frustrating players with its difficult encounters, but rather than turn me off, it motivates me to keep playing.
articles.body: I would not call the time I’m having with Hollow Knight: Silksong “fun,” and yet I’m still playing. In the depths of The Marrow, the second major area of Silksong, there’s a particularly nasty midboss. I eventually beat him, but my reward wasn’t a new ability, item, or a bench where I could rest and save my progress. All I got was pain, suffering, and death. In Silksong, the only way out is through, but the “through” is a tunnel lined with spikes that occasionally spew gouts of flame. I should have given up right then and there, but I have not abandoned Silksong the same way I do other unfun games. For the life of me, I couldn’t figure out why I didn’t just put Silksong down and chalk it up as another “not for me” game the way Hollow Knight just wasn’t for me. I enjoy Metroidvanias a great deal — Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown was one of my favorite games of last year. And for Silksong, I wanted to try Team Cherry’s work again and see if it would finally click. It has, and it’s because of the community (and a lot of spite). I came to Hollow Knight late, long after the buzz about it had left my social media circle. With Silksong, I’m playing it at the same time as everyone else. My social media feed is full of people who love the game much more than I do, posting tips, commiserating about its moments of bullshit (hello, lantern fruit pogo platforming), and gushing over the adorable Sherma. [Media: “I have only known Sherma for a day and a half…” When I post lamenting the game’s bullshit, I get excited messages from my friends giving me advice on what I should do next. It’s like we’re all doing our own personal let’s plays together while being in each other’s chats. It feels good. I am not alone in my misery, and better yet, I’ve got friends to help. For Silksong it’s worked in such a way that’s kept me playing longer than I would have if I were going this alone. This kind of collective, collaborative gaming experience has also taught me a new trick: taking a break. I’ve never been the kind of gamer that stops playing when I can’t overcome an obstacle. I either do something else in the game or keep running at my problem until I figure it out. Now, when I feel myself getting even the slightest bit mad because I was so close (or I thought I was so close) to surmounting a challenge, I turn off the game and come back later. It’s so silly that, once again, the “touch grass” people are right, but the strategy has gotten me through some of the game’s most egregious moments. (If the vendor Shakra wants to leave her post in Greymoor because of something I did, that’s fine. But taking her bench with her that’s in a room right before a brutal combat gauntlet is a unique and dastardly flavor of Silksong bullshit.) [Image: You see this fight? Bullshit. And when I overcome that bullshit, I get this incredible frisson of thrill. When I easily beat a boss in fewer tries than I’m used to, I feel godly. I’m actually quite tickled to hear Team Cherry is working to nerf some of the early bosses, because those were fine. (It’s the damn pogo platforming!) I’m pretty sure I’m going to finish Silksong and whatever I feel at the end of that journey will be more like relief than joy. Silksong has shown me I don’t need to feel “happiness” or “joy” to continue playing a game. I just want to feel something — even if that something is pure spite.

articles.summary: Hunting Animals are a subsection of the list of Animals you can find and identify in Grand Theft Auto 6. There are 61 different types of Hunting Animals that
articles.body:
Hunting Animals are a subsection of the list of Animals you can find and identify in Grand Theft Auto 6. There are 61 different types of Hunting Animals that can be found across Leonida County.

To identify any type of animal you come across, you can first target a creature by locking on with L2 / LT , and then hold down R1 / RB while the target is in range to Study it. If you can hold down the input long enough before the animal moves out of range, it will be correctly identifed, and added to the Animals section under the Progress tab.

Since animals are often wary of humans, you can also identify them from a distance using the scopes of your Binoculars (Hold L1 / LB to bring up the Weapon Wheel and select the Binoculars in the bottom right corner), or use a scoped rifle weapon, either of which allows you to use the Identify prompt at range without having to lock on.

Below you'll find a complete list of all Hunting Animals in GTA6 in the order they are listed in the Progress tracker of the main menu. Be sure to check out IGN's Official Interactive Map of GTA6 for heat maps of all types of animals!

articles.body:
Fishing Animals are a subsection of the list of Animals you can find and identify by catching in Grand Theft Auto 6. There are 35 different types of Fishing Animals that can be found across Leonida County.

Unlike identifying other animals by targeting them, these fish can be identified by catching them with a Fishing Rod in waters all over the map.

Below you'll find a complete list of all Fishing Animals in GTA6 in the order they are listed in the Progress tracker of the main menu. Be sure to check out IGN's Official Interactive Map of GTA6 for heat maps of all types of animals!

There are a few steps to fishing in GTAVI. You can select a rod from the Loadout inventory by pressing and holding L1 / LB and shuffling through the held items until you find a rod.

With it in hand, you’ll do the following to cast:

Hold L2 / LT (you’ll continue to hold while the line is out).

Press R2 / RT and release it to cast. The longer you hold it down, the further the cast.

Slowly use the right thumbstick ( Right Stick ) to reel the line in, which can attract fish.

When you get a bite, press R2/RT to hook the fish.

Reel in the fish and use the left thumbstick ( Left Stick ) to adjust how you’re pulling the rod. Ideally, you’ll pull against the direction the fish is swimming. So, if the fish goes right, pull the rod to the left and vice versa. The more effectively you tire the fish, the fast you’ll be able to reel in the fish.

Aquatic Animals are a subsection of the list of Animals you can find and identify in Grand Theft Auto 6. There are 18 different kinds of large marine life that can't be fished that can be discovered in Leonida County.

To identify any type of animal you come across, you can first target a creature by locking on with L2 / LT , and then hold down R1 / RB while the target is in range to Study it. If you can hold down the input long enough before the animal moves out of range, it will be correctly identified, and added to the Animals section under the Progress tab.

Since animals are often wary of humans, you can also identify them from a distance using the scopes of your Binoculars (Hold L1 / LB to bring up the Weapon Wheel and select the Binoculars in the bottom right corner), or use a scoped rifle weapon, either of which allows you to use the Identify prompt at range without having to lock on.

Below you'll find a complete list of all Aquatic Animals in GTA6 in the order they are listed in the Progress tracker of the main menu. Be sure to check out IGN's Official Interactive Map of GTA6 for heat maps of all types of animals!

The largest of all tuna fish, the massive bluefin swims throughout Leonida's deep oceans, propelled by powerful muscles and a big appetite. It is one of the few warm-blooded fish, and a popular ingredient in sushi.

Where to Find: Key Lento, along the reefs to the south of the key.

The goliath grouper is a large saltwater fish with mottled, brownish scales, and favors tropical coastal waters and reefs.

The Atlantic sailfish can be found in the cold, deep waters to the east of Leonida. With its huge dorsal fin, needle-like snout, and vivid scales, it is one of the region's most recognizable fish species.

Where to Find: Key Lento - Along the reefs and shipwrecks south of the Key.

A common sight in coastal waters to the north and west, the Atlantic stingray is dwarfed by the region's other ray species. It defends itself with a serrated tail, but poses little threat to humans.

Where to Look: Key Lento - Guarding the reefs and sandbars south of the Key.

One of the region's smaller shark species, the blacktip shark can be seen in the ocean west of Leonida, and gets its name from the distinctive coloration of its fin tips.

Where to Look - All sandy coastlines of Leonida (except Vice City), concentrated in sandy beach areas like Keys around Mile Zero Air Station.

The blue land crab can be observed all around Leonida's coastline, where it makes its home in burrows near the water. Recognizable by the bluish tint on its carapace.

Short, sturdy, and highly aggressive towards humans, the bull shark is an apex predator and can be observed throughout the waters surrounding Leonida.

Where to Look - Key Lento: in the deep ocean west of the key, often found just to the south of the Nuestra Señora Del Ocio you explore as part of the main story.

The giant oceanic manta ray glides through the deep oceans, propelled by its massive, wing-like fins. It has an enormous brain and is thought to be very intelligent.

Where to Look - Key Lento: Found in the waters southeast of the key, often near the Nuestra Señora de la Noche shipwreck by the sandbars.

The world's largest hammerhead shark, the great hammerhead is an apex predator found in the waters surrounding Leonida. It has little interest in humans.

Where to Look - Catlan Key: Easily found in a large circular pond at the Vice City Oceanarium in Catalan Key. You can also find them in a small pond at Farmer Scrumpy's Red Apple Orchard near SR-73 in western Manifest Canyon, north of Port Gellhorn.

Known for its mottled, brightly-colored scales, the koi was created through the selective breeding of domestic carp. Many can be found in man-made freshwater ponds, serving as status symbols for the elite.

Where to Look - Sandbars, Belpoint: Unlike the Blue Land Crab, the Stone Crab can be found exclusively along the beaches of the sandbars located west of both Gellhorn and Capri along Leonida's western reaches.

Found on Leonida's western beaches, the Leonida stone crab is gray-brown species whose claws are considered a culinary delicacy.

The moon jellyfish prefers deeper waters but can occasionally be seen around the Leonida coast. It is translucent, and lacks the long tentacles common to many other jellyfish species.

Immediately recognizable by its signature bill, the North Atlantic swordfish is a large, predatory fish found in waters all around Leonida, favoring the deep ocean.

The shy, docile nurse shark favors ocean reefs, but can be seen gathering in large groups near the coast at night. Recognizable by the barbels that dangle above its jaws.

Famed for its bizarre appearance and potentially lethal sting, the Portuguese man o' war can be spotted floating on the ocean surface from the southeast to the northwest. To be avoided.

Easily identified by its long tail and the white spots that adorn its back, the spotted eagle ray can be sighted around the Leonida coast.

A huge nocturnal predator, the tiger shark is found throughout Leonida's oceans. Easily identified by the stripes decorating its skin.

Where to Look - Key Lento: This bright blue fish tends to lurk along the reefs and shipwrecks in the southwest past Key Lento in the deeper waters.

A bright blue fish with a striking yellow tail, this damselfish favors warmer waters to the south and west of Leonida.

articles.title: Starting From Zero Walkthrough - GTA 6 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Jason and Lucia have escaped Mendez's task force again, but their longtime enemy isn't giving up. They’re not either. In this official IGN GTA
articles.body:
Jason and Lucia have escaped Mendez's task force again, but their longtime enemy isn't giving up. They’re not either. In this official IGN GTA 6 Chapter 4 walkthrough for Starting from Zero, learn about this mission's major choice, outcomes, and more.

This mission begins right as the previous mission, Sunset, ends. The opening cutscene shows Jason and Lucia at new lows. Their accounts are frozen. Their backs are up against a wall.

The decision you have here is important – though the choices available to you depend on Jason and Lucia’s relationship level . For instance, if you have a high level with either Hot Together (4/4) or Crazy in Love (3/4), you won’t even see this option . For those of you who do, think carefully before deciding. Below are notes on the outcomes of what they impact:

If the relationship level is Partners in Crime (2/4), You have two choices:

If You Want… ( Square / Y ) – Agree to the breakup.

Lu… No ( Cross / A ) – Jason and Lucia stay in a relationship.

If you choose to keep the couple together , Lucia comments that neither of them has been trying to make each other happy. Jason persists, arguing that they haven’t exactly had time amid all the madness, before asking if she wants to give it another shot. Lucia agrees to try again, and they receive a relationship boost.

If you choose to break Lucia and Jason up , Jason is apprehensive but agrees. She picks up on his hesitation and asks again. You get a second chance to save the relationship – this decision is final.

Maybe For the Best ( Square / Y ) – Jason and Lucia break up.

If you take too long to answer here, Jason automatically tells Lucia he wants to stay together, saving their relationship.

If you end things , Jason agrees to go separate ways, including with Tomás – he wants her to raise him by herself as he can’t commit to fatherhood. Lucia thanks him for trying to make it work for as long as he did. Their relationship level changes to Breakdown, which cannot be changed.

If Jason and Lucia’s relationship level is Running on Empty (1/4), Lucia floats the idea of breaking up to Jason. You have two choices:

If you take too long to answer, Jason automatically agrees to end their relationship.

If you choose to keep them together , Lucia comments that neither of them has been trying in their relationship. Jason persists – they’ve been distracted by a lot – before asking if she wants to try again. Lucia agrees and they receive a relationship boost.

If you break Lucia and Jason up , Jason agrees to end their relationship amicably. He wants her to raise Tomás alone – he can’t be the father their son needs. Lucia thanks him for trying anyway. The decision is final and their relationship level changes to Breakdown, which cannot be changed.

No matter what you decide, Lucia and Jason get in touch with Andrea. Raul said she had the hard drive. She does, and she’s not happy to hear from the two. She tells them to meet her at Aqua Stadium, and fast.

You don’t have a ton of time to meet with Andrea before she bolts. So long as you make an effort to go directly to the stadium, though, you should catch her. Start by finding a car. There’s a truck with an advanced alarm near the trashed car Lucia was sitting in, but anything with an alarm is a dangerous gamble. You’re already Wanted. If you walk around the warehouse, you’ll find another truck with lackluster security that makes for a good ride. Find whatever works for you, though, and get on the road. Cops are everywhere. As Jason and Lucia talk on the ride to Aqua Stadium, keep an eye out for any tailing cop cars. If you get caught on your way to Andrea, she will not meet you at the stadium. If you approach while actively being chased or if you take too long getting to the stadium, Tap to Reveal .

Don’t forget, if you see the awareness meter from the other side of the road or from behind you, all you need to do to keep a cop from identifying Jason and Lucia is break line of sight. You can duck in the car when it’s stopped (and only when it’s stopped) by holding Circle / B , or you can move around another car or structure to break the line of sight.

If you made it to the stadium safely, look for Andrea at the heavily graffitied Aqua Stadium. Jason mentions checking the bleachers. As soon as you walk around the base of the bleachers a cutscene with Andrea begins if she’s there. It’s not long and she leaves quickly.

The go bag is a decent next step. As you move through the stadium you might spot cop cars in the parking lot. There’s a Seashark on the west end of the stadium bleachers, but keep in mind that cops patrol the water too and Seasharks don’t provide any sort of cover. A car provides better protection against being identified.

Make your way to the storage facility once you’ve found your preferred vehicle. When you reach the facility, a cutscene starts and Lucia receives yet another text from Mattia. This time, he’s allegedly offering to help if they meet at the High Life Hotel bar. Jason and Lucia make a plan and head over.

Lucia is going in first. Take the elevator to the bar, Acai Dreams, and follow the hostess to Mattia’s table. The view is indeed great, just like the hostess said, but Mattia isn’t at the table. Two bodyguards meet you and take the package to their boss. The threat of the withheld hard drive doesn’t have much weight when Lucia is dangled over the railing. You can choose to answer them or hold out until Lucia fights back. It doesn’t matter either way as they pat down Lucia and take her phone and send a photo to Jason. Now, back as Jason, use the elevator to join the meeting. Not long after arriving, Jason and Lucia get bags thrown over their heads.

Sometime later, Jason and Lucia find themselves in a cold, quiet room. You can look around, but it’s difficult to see anything with the bag. Another cutscene begins as their captor, Giorgio, removes their hood and offers them a present: it’s Mattia. Giorgio hands you his gun and allows you to decide Mattia’s fate. You can:

Make your choice. Your action impacts the initial moments of the cutscene, but nothing else. Giorgio leads Jason and Lucia out of the meat fridge. Follow him to the balcony where he explains his plan for the pair. Giorgio is willing to let Jason and Lucia live so long as they help him get his shipments of drugs back. You’ll live with him in his luxurious apartment until the job is complete.

Follow Giorgio’s bodyguard, Dardan, through the penthouse and up your new room. Jason and Lucia go to sleep, ending the mission and Chapter 4. Next is Chapter 5's first mission: Bird in the Hand .

articles.title: The Outrage Over Jason Buying Lucia Flowers Is GTA 6's Dumbest Controversy
articles.summary: Some corners of the internet are furious Rockstar has apparently turned its crime simulator into a game about being a considerate boyfriend, while others are discovering that Jason Duval might just be the perfect man.
articles.body:
Of all the things I expected Grand Theft Auto 6 to cause arguments about, whether or not a man should buy his girlfriend flowers was pretty low on the list. Yet some corners of the internet are furious that Rockstar has apparently turned its crime simulator into a game about being a considerate boyfriend, while others are discovering that Jason Duval might just be the perfect man – a sentence I never thought I’d write about a Grand Theft Auto protagonist.

As well as the usual GTA activities of stealing cars, shooting people, and generally being a menace to society, GTA 6 gives players the option to nurture the relationship between its two protagonists, Jason and Lucia. It's especially prevalent at the start of the game, where you can renovate their home, buy Lucia flowers, pick out clothes and accessories for her while shopping, bring her drinks, open car doors, and even hold her hand while walking around Leonida. I think it's all rather sweet, especially when you consider that these two are also quite happy to commit armed robberies together. Couples who crime together, stay together. (That's not a spoiler; that's me high on hopium as I play through the story.)

In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023

Crucially, all of this romantic housekeeping is optional. The game certainly prompts you to nurture the relationship, especially early on when we're just finding out who Jason and Lucia are. But when the button-press to hold hands or show affection pops up, you're free to ignore it. Over time, this will cause the relationship to cool to the point where eventually they become platonic partners in crime, but they're still very much in it together.

Showing affection is also not specific to Jason either – once you're through Chapter 1, which is heavily focused on the army vet, and deeper into the game where you spend more time as both characters, they can both choose to show the other affection – or not, if you so desire. You choose how much effort they want to put into Jason and Lucia’s relationship, and the game responds accordingly. You can make them the sort of disgustingly loved-up couple who make everyone around them feel slightly ill, or let their relationship cool into something more businesslike. No one is being forced to play house.

From a quick browse of social media, and, in particular, X, you'll see posts reading, "RIP GTA. Killed by women. Like so many before," from @trackthedecline. User @ExoGhost writes, "GTA 6 has a mission where you need to buy flowers for Lucia. This game is such woke slop. It's so obvious it was made by women." And then there's @5jmxgz, who claims, "gta 6 lowk the biggest flop ever, we waited 13 years for a literal cuck simulator."

Grand Theft Auto 6 cemented itself as the most successful entertainment launch of all-time , making $3.79 billion in just one day.

For some players, the problem seems to be that they’ve waited 13 years for a new GTA game, only to find themselves assembling furniture and picking up groceries. There’s a reasonable argument buried somewhere in there about whether mundane domestic activities are what people want from a series built on criminal excess and absolute freedom. If you spend your actual life doing chores, perhaps coming home to do more of them in a video game isn’t particularly appealing? The pace of Chapter 1 feels like deliberate decision from Rockstar to subvert what people expect from GTA, and I think it's that that's causing at least some of the reaction, because once you move onto Chapter 2 and beyond, the only chores you're really doing is putting cups in the sink, opening car doors, and getting your significant other a snack now and again. No one is cleaning the oven or pulling lint out of the dryer.

However, some of the complaints go considerably further, treating the idea of Jason showing any kind of affection or consideration for Lucia as an attack on masculinity itself. Some have described the game as a “cuck simulator” while reacting to Jason running errands for Lucia. Apparently, buying your girlfriend something nice is now a threat to civilization. Someone should probably warn the florists.

For me, GTA 6 is Rockstar at its subversive best. While internet conflict raged over whether or not games were getting too “woke” and that the heroes were becoming too “soft,” Rockstar gave us a strong, straight, masculine guy with a hot girlfriend. The only catch? You have to put in the work that goes with that. You need to put effort into the relationship to keep the hot girlfriend, you need to go to the gym to stay buff, you need to contribute to the household finances.

Some X users are seeing the positives in Jason and Lucia's dynamic, and the warmth shared between them. "When he said 'you and Tommy are the only family I need', then went ahead to include her mom because he knows how important she is to her. Yep Jason Duval is not just a green flag but the greenest forest," says @keiuzuki. It's a sentiment shared by many others, who are already creating collages, montages, and memes dedicated to Mr Duval.

For plenty of female players, Jason’s appeal isn’t just that he’s attractive, capable, or willing to commit a little light felony in the name of love. It’s that he pays attention. He notices things. He makes an effort. And while the bar for romantic male behavior probably shouldn’t be somewhere around buying flowers and remembering to open a car door, there’s something undeniably appealing about a game that makes those little gestures feel important. The man has a criminal record, questionable career prospects, and presumably several outstanding warrants, but at least he remembers to buy you a lemonade.

There’s also a particularly funny subset of women watching their real-life partners enthusiastically renovate a fictional house, buy fictional flowers, and take their fictional girlfriend shopping, while wondering when exactly that energy might make its way into their actual relationship. Imagine watching your husband spend three hours choosing the perfect paint color for a woman made of polygons while the dishwasher has needed emptying since Tuesday.

Others have even suggested that GTA 6 is having a positive effect on their relationships, with men apparently taking inspiration from Jason’s behavior and becoming more thoughtful partners themselves. Rockstar may have inadvertently created the world’s most expensive couples’ therapy.

"My husband has been playing GTA 6 and took a break to run to the get food," tells Threads user monroecammack. "He came back with ice cream and flowers for me and said 'if I have to get Lucia flowers, then I have to get flowers for you too' and I - ." One reply humurously replied with, "OMG THAT IS WHY MY HUSBAND RANDOMLY GOT ME FLOWERS YESTERDAY."

And perhaps that’s the most interesting thing about this whole argument. GTA has always been about giving players the freedom to indulge in fantasies, whether that’s becoming a criminal kingpin, owning an absurd collection of supercars, or escaping the police in increasingly ridiculous ways. GTA 6 simply adds another fantasy to the list: being in a loving, functional relationship, which is truly the most unrealistic thing Rockstar has ever put in one of its games.

To reiterate, Lucia isn’t just sitting around waiting for Jason to bring her presents. She’s a playable protagonist with her own agency, and the relationship mechanics allow both characters to show affection and consideration for one another. This isn’t necessarily about a man serving a woman. It’s about two people making an effort.

Nobody is suggesting that GTA 6 should replace actual relationship advice, and buying your girlfriend flowers isn’t going to magically fix a failing relationship. But there’s something fascinating about watching a game famous for its violence accidentally spark a conversation about emotional labor, affection, and what people expect from their partners. If nothing else, it’s rather telling that in a game where you can steal cars, rob banks, and murder people, one of the most controversial things Jason Duval can do is be nice to his girlfriend. Apparently, Grand Theft Auto is fine. Grand Theft Affection is where some draw the line. Rockstar has made it clear that maintaining their relationship requires effort from both sides. Which makes the outrage over Jason buying flowers even stranger, unless I've missed the part where basic consideration became a gender-specific skill.

Rachel Weber is the Head of Editorial Development at IGN and an elder millennial. She's been a professional nerd since 2006 when she got her start on Official PlayStation Magazine in the UK, and has since worked for GamesIndustry.Biz, Rolling Stone and GamesRadar. She loves horror, horror movies, horror games, Red Dead Redemption 2, and her Love and Deepspace boyfriends.

articles.title: Hollow Knight: Silksong Dev Gets Into the Direct Business With Cherry Time! Special Presentation
articles.summary: Team Cherry has announced an upcoming Cherry Time! Special Presentation, during which it will issue an update on the hotly anticipated Hollow Knight: Silksong expansion, Sea of Sorrow.
articles.body:
Team Cherry has announced an upcoming Cherry Time! Special Presentation, during which it will issue an update on the hotly anticipated Hollow Knight: Silksong expansion, Sea of Sorrow.

The Australian developer said this YouTube presentation will include “a bunch of exciting announcements” in addition to the Sea of Sorrow update, sparking speculation that the developer may be ready to discuss what’s next. There is also speculation around what the Sea of Sorrow update will be. Could it be a shadow drop? A release date announcement for before the end of the year? Or, perhaps, word that Sea of Sorrow is somehow three times as big as expected so it's delayed and now a full-on sequel? Roll the dice!

Cherry Time! Special Presentation is set for 7am PT / 10am ET / 3pm UK time on Friday, November 27.

Hollow Knight Silksong Physical Edition - Everything Included

Team Cherry teased the nautically themed Sea of Sorrow in December last year with a 2026 release window. It's free for all players. As part of the DLC announcement, Team Cherry said Hollow Knight: Silksong had sold more than 7 million copies since going on sale in September 2025, and had millions more playing on Xbox Game Pass.

"It’s a truly staggering number of players, more than we could have ever expected (enough to crash all of the storefronts!)," Team Cherry said at the time. "Watching the community grow, seeing the amazing art, the mods, the unexpected strategies, and the support between players through the game’s challenges has been hugely rewarding for us here at home. Your continued enthusiasm remains a massive motivator as we work towards expanding the game even further."

IGN's Hollow Knight: Silksong review scored the game 9/10. We said: "Hollow Knight: Silksong is packed full of sharp platforming, enticing exploration, and nail-biting combat that's all unapologetically challenging in just the right way."

articles.title: The Witcher 3 and Assassin's Creed 'Reset Player Expectations' for Open-World Action RPGs, So the Fable Reboot Devs Had to Look Beyond the Original Trilogy for Inspiration
articles.summary: Why has the Fable reboot taken so long to develop? There are a number of reasons, but part of it is that expectations around open-world action RPGs were reset by various competing games over the past decade.
articles.body:
Why has the Fable reboot taken so long to develop? There are a number of reasons, but part of it is that expectations around open-world action RPGs were reset by various competing games over the past decade.

Work on Fable reportedly started in 2016, and only now, 10 years later, is it near release. It’s suffered a tumultuous development but, unlike some other costly Microsoft gaming projects, it has avoided closure amid sweeping layoffs and restructuring at Xbox.

In a new interview with GamesIndustry.biz , Playground Games co-founder and Fable general manager Ralph Fulton touched on the trials and tribulations Fable has endured over the years. Playground set up a new team to make Fable in addition to its hugely popular racing game franchise, Forza Horizon, and set out to make a game in a genre it had no prior experience with. And Fable is a big role-playing game, with all the bells and whistles you'd expect. So, Fable isn’t technically a debut game from Playground, but it sort of is.

In terms of what’s changed, Fulton said that technology had “advanced” during development, pointing to a reset of player expectations with the release of CD Projekt’s fantasy RPG masterpiece The Witcher 3 and then Assassin’s Creed’s move towards the RPG genre.

This, Fulton explained, meant that Playground had to look beyond the original Fable trilogy for inspiration to ensure it created a reboot that would meet modern open-world standards.

“In 2015, The Witcher 3 redefined what an open-world action RPG looks like and became the gold standard,” Fulton explained. “And after that bar was raised, the Assassin's Creed franchise changed into this more modern iteration with Origins, Odyssey, and Valhalla, and became like a quasi-RPG.

“All of these games continue to reset player expectations, which means I think looking only to the original Fable trilogy for inspiration would leave us lacking in terms of what the modern audience, the modern marketplace, expects.”

Despite this, the scope of Fable actually decreased over time, with the project starting with “an enormous potential scope.” In August, Playground confirmed that Fable’s main quest will take around 20 hours to beat , with an additional 15-20 hours of side and open-world exploration content available. Howlongtobeat has the original 2004 Fable 's main quest clocking in at about 12-and-a-half hours. Fable 2 isn't much longer at 13 hours , and Fable 3 inches just further past that at 13-and-a-half hours . So, the Fable reboot is shaping up to be the longest in the series.

Fable is set for launch on February 23, 2027, across PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X and S.

articles.title: I Can Speak Whale Walkthrough - Disney Dreamlight Valley Guide - IGN
articles.summary: I Can Speak Whale, alternately spelled as I CaaAAAannn SpeeeaAAAAAAKKkk WWWHHAAAAALEeee!!!, is a Quest in Disney Dreamlight Valley's Keepsake Sea
articles.body:
I Can Speak Whale, alternately spelled as I CaaAAAannn SpeeeaAAAAAAKKkk WWWHHAAAAALEeee!!!, is a Quest in Disney Dreamlight Valley's Keepsake Sea expansion . After freeing Captain Hook from Donut Island during the previous Quest, Donut of Destiny , you learned that Hook may know something about the remaining Keepsakes in Candy Cove which you need to claim to complete the next Trial!

Talk to Captain Hook, who will be on the right side of Sweetwater Wharf, next to his ruined ship. Meg will show up and warn you that Hook is up to no good, but, unfortunately, you need to cooperate with him to get the treasure map back.

Gather the following materials to restore Hook's ship:

Rock Candy x 10 - mined from Rock Spots anywhere in Candy Cove

Sherbet Cane Straw x 5 - grown from Seeds purchased at Goofy's Stall in Frosted Fjord

Gummy Bean x 15 - picked from the ground in any area of Candy Cove

Igloo Crab x 4 - fished from white or blue ripples anywhere in Candy Cove

Once you have gathered all of the materials, give them to Captain Hook.

Captain Hook tells you that the Whirlpool you need is in the out in the water where the Narwhal that sank his ship is lurking. You won't be able to lure her away unless you know someone who speaks whale - and, fortunately, Dory can do just that!

Using the Wardrobe Menu, equip Dory as your Adventure Companion and then talk to her. She confirms that she can indeed speak whale!

Turn into your merfolk form and swim out to the Narwhal, who is in the water on the right side of Sweetwater Wharf. Talk to her, and Dory relays that the Narwhal is currently too hungry to move.

Cook her the following meals using any Cooking Station, such as the one near the Wishing Well in Shortcake Summit:

Gummy Bean x 2 - picked from the ground in all areas of Candy Cove

Oyster x 2 - foraged on Dazzle Beach, purchased at Goofy's Stall in the Frosted Fjord

Sherbet Cane Straw x 2 - grown from Seeds purchased at Goofy's Stall in the Frosted Fjord

Any Grain x 2 - any easy option is Wheat, grown from Seeds purchased at Goofy's Stall in the Peaceful Meadow

Make sure you have all four Meals in your Inventory. Then, return to the Narwhal and give her all of the Meals.

Now fed, the Narwhal happily moves out of the way - revealing a Whirlpool behind her that you can dive right into!

In your merfolk form, enter the whirlpool behind where the Narwhal was swimming. You will find yourself in a small area of the Dessert Depths that has been cut off by a magical barrier.

Some Cookie Cutters are floating in the water in front of you. Interact with them, and the first Sunken Echo Puzzle will appear!

Read the note in front of the puzzle. This time, you'll be following a recipe to help the Legendary Adventurer make cookies!

Open the refrigerator in the top left corner of the puzzle. Take out the butter, eggs, ginger, and jam.

Open the storage cabinet in the bottom left corner of the puzzle. Take out the sugar, salt, chocolate, and flour.

Interact with the pile of bowls in front of the Adventurer and their guardian. Add the butter, eggs, sugar, salt, and flour.

Three bowls will appear in front of the Legendary Adventurer and their guardian. Interact with any of the three bowls and add the chocolate, ginger, and jam.

Pick up the bowls and place them in the oven on the right side of the puzzle.

Pick up the cookies. (Sadly, you do not actually get to keep them.)

The puzzle is solved, and it disappears!

Read the note. It's another logic puzzle! This time, you need to figure out which house the Legendary Adventurer's friends live in, and deliver the right flavor of cookie to each one. The note gives you the following hints:

The lookout lives in a house with a red mailbox and wants jam cookies

The bosun lives in a house with a pink carpet and wants gingerbread cookies

The first mate lives in a house with a snowman with a top hat nearby and wants chocolate cookies

Pick up the green box on top of the stack in the Legendary Adventurer's wagon. It has jam cookies.

Give the jam cookies to the house straight across from the Adventurer. (It is possible you may encounter a glitch that causes the mailbox to not appear properly red, but this is the correct house.)

Pick up the blue box from the wagon. It has gingerbread cookies.

Give the gingerbread cookies to the house to the right of the Legendary Adventurer, which has a pink carpet.

Pick up the red from the wagon. There are chocolate cookies in this box.

Give the chocolate cookies to the house on the left, with the top hat snowman in front of it.

Once all cookies have been delivered, the puzzle disappears!

Once the second puzzle has been solved, the Bottled Cookie Cutters appear in front of you. Pick them up and the barrier around the area disappears!

Return to the surface via the whirlpool and swim back to Sweetwater Wharf. Oh no! Captain Hook's ship is gone! But Megara is there, so talk to her.

Megara says that Hook left as soon as you entered the Whirlpool, but says that you should focus on awakening the next Guardian rather than chasing him. From the dock of Sweetwater Wharf, summon your ship and sail to the right until you reach the Grotto of Expression.

Once in the Grotto, place the Bottled Art Supplies, Bottled Hat, and Bottled Cookie Cutters on the pedestal in front of the Guardian. She will wake up!

Talk to the Guardian of Expression. She tells you that she is the last obstacle you must overcome before reaching the lost Kingdom of Oublié. The Quest concludes here, and you must pass her Trial in the next one!

articles.title: This GTA 6 Radio Station Represents Its Florida-Inspired Setting Perfectly
articles.summary: Southern hip-hop deserves its respect in rap history and GTA 6 celebrates it with its own radio station full of bangers from Outkast, T.I., Trick Daddy, Gucci Mane, and so many more.
articles.body:
Radio stations have always been a staple of Grand Theft Auto, filled with licensed (and some original) songs alongside crazy-ass talk shows. GTA 6 is unprecedented in this field, with its massive tracklist and over-the-top on-air personalities. But we all have the music genres we gravitate towards when picking out a station, and the one I'm rarely ever changing is Dirty South Classics – basically a playlist of the Southern hip-hop bangers I grew up listening to. It's also a thematic fit for GTA 6's setting of Leonida, an obvious parallel to the state of Florida.

While you traditionally wouldn't consider South Florida or the city of Miami part of the American South, the rest of Florida is largely culturally aligned with the region's states like Georgia, Mississippi, and parts of Texas (namely Houston). These are key distinctions to make in the context of music, especially what we consider Southern hip-hop – colloquially known as 'dirty south' hip-hop, hence the station name. Deep bass, rattling hi-hats, catchy melodies with instrumentals that either align with aggressive trap beats or the more soulful funk; characteristics of the genre that you hear throughout Dirty South Classics.

Because of its importance as a subgenre, and as a prominent cultural touchstone of the region that GTA 6 is trying to portray, it got its own dedicated station separate from VCRR, which is for more contemporary rap hits. So, admittedly, Dirty South Classics laser-targets oldheads who scrapped in the schoolyard in the early/mid 2000s – damn, I guess I really am unc now, huh. Hell, the station is hosted by Trick Daddy and Trina, two major figures in the Southern rap game from Miami (with interstitials from Gucci Mane himself). Just in the first few hours of my playthrough of GTA 6, I kept thinking to myself, 'They put this song in the game?!' And they all took me back to a very specific time and place as I rapped along off the top of the brain like I was a youngin' all over again.

I'm glad GTA 6 went with Outkast's "Player's Ball" instead of the Atlanta-based duo's more well-known hits. It has the quintessential sound of a classic Southern hip-hop track with a bold bassline and funky instrumentals rounded out with Andre 3000's falsetto hook. This particular style can be heard throughout their debut album "Southernplayalisticadillacmuzik" (1994) – although Outkast's sound changed in interesting ways afterward and exploded in popularity, it's still my favorite record of theirs.

On the other end of the genre spectrum, I can’t believe I'm hearing Dem Franchize Boyz' "White Tee" in a game in the year 2026. It was their first song to break containment in 2004 and it's an ode to, well, the universality of the plain white t-shirt – affordable, easy to match in any outfit, and helpful in keeping a low profile, as covered in the song's lyrics. This especially resonated in the era of tall tees in my neighborhood, but I still don't understand the hostility toward throwbacks.

Maybe I shouldn't have been listening to them when I was a kid, but Three 6 Mafia's "Side 2 Side" was my favorite song from the Memphis-based trio. That dark, melancholic cello melody that runs throughout the track is undeniably catchy and Juicy J's flow on the last verse goes so hard. I'm a little surprised GTA 6 didn't go with the more popular remix featuring Bow Wow, but I am glad because the original version here is damn near perfect.

Lastly, I have to shout out "Knuck If You Buck" by Crime Mob and Lil Scrappy , the universal fight or flight mode anthem. Its dark, aggressive sound and trunk-knocking bass makes you feel invincible, and those first four notes activate any 30-something-year-old who had to square up and run the fade at school in a moment's notice.

I'm scratching the surface of the Dirty South Classics radio station, only four of the 39 songs which include hits from Big Tymers, T.I., Juvenile, Mike Jones (who? Mike Jones!) and so many more – that's not counting club bangers from Gucci Mane, Lil' Jon, Petey Pablo, among others. And it's just one of the 20 music stations featured in GTA 6 that include traditional Latin music, foreign covers of big hits, deep country, a roster of top-40 pop hits, and more. So, it's pretty nice that the biggest game in the world can also be a celebration of music, especially for a culture attached to its own setting.

articles.title: One of GTA 6's Best Features Was Actually Planned for GTA: Vice City, Reveals Ex-Rockstar Dev
articles.summary: GTA 6's headphones mechanic was originally planned to be included in the original GTA: Vice City, according to a former Rockstar Games employee.
articles.body:
GTA 6's headphones mechanic was originally planned to be included in the original GTA: Vice City, according to a former Rockstar Games employee.

Ex-Rockstar Games dev Obbe Vermeji revealed that the headphones feature was cut from GTA: Vice City due to a technical reason, and they had even created an icon for it. It's unclear what the technical reason was, but Vice City's version likely would've come in the form of a Walkman or cassette player, given it was set in the 80s. GTA 6's version, however, comes with a smartphone and a pair of AirPods.

The feature is pretty incredible, because you can listen to music and podcasts wherever you go. You no longer have to sit in the car to finish a song; you can just get out, put your headphones in, and turn on the radio station you were just listening to. And when combined with combat encounters, it can have some thrilling results. Last night, In the Air Tonight came on as I approached a gang hideout, creating an incredibly cinematic moment for me.

This is the best game ever made dude — Cade Onder (@Cade_Onder) November 25, 2026

It doesn't always have to lead to some epic moment, though. It's great for working out in-game, learning about the world and lore of GTA via podcasts and talk shows, and much more. A lot of effort has been packed into creating GTA 6's in-game media, and the headphones allow you to make full use of it. The only downside is that you can't make any kind of custom playlists. Presumably, this is because Rockstar wants players to organically discover music from the radio stations instead of curating the songs they already know and love.

The option would be nice, but personally, there are so many great songs I may have never heard if GTA's radio stations didn't expose me to them. Maybe a future update or the inevitable online mode will include a playlist option, but it could be a while before we see such a thing.

articles.title: 'It Would Be Absolutely Incredible' — Hideki Kamiya Wants to Make a New Castlevania Game With Konami
articles.summary: Hideki Kamiya, the mind behind Devil May Cry, Bayonetta, and Okami, wants to make a new Castlevania game, saying his team at CLOVERS could make something “absolutely incredible.”
articles.body:
Hideki Kamiya, the mind behind Devil May Cry , Bayonetta , and Okami , wants to make a new Castlevania game, saying his team at CLOVERS could make something "absolutely incredible" alongside Konami.

Hideki Kamiya is back in the saddle at CLOVERS, his independent game studio made up of former CLOVER staff who are currently hard at work on the Okami sequel . He made the company’s independent status extremely clear in his latest YouTube video , reminding excited fans to stop asking him about Capcom-owned franchises (or even sequels to games like God Hand , since he had no part in its development).

Given CLOVERS’ status as an independent company that’s already working with a major developer in Capcom, Kamiya floated ideas for future collaborations with other big developers once the Okami sequel is out in the world. One of those ideas was a partnership with Konami for a Castlevania game, which he promised would be “incredible,” if it actually ends up happening.

“Since we’re independent and don’t have any outside funding, we want to stay on good terms — or rather, collaborate — with various companies and keep doing interesting things,” he explained. “Of course, I want to keep building a good relationship with Capcom, and naturally, I’d like to be on good terms with Nintendo, too.

“...Maybe I could make a new Getsufumaden with Konami. Oh, and Castlevania. If we made it, it would be absolutely incredible, so please, let us take the job. I am a bit busy right now, though,” he laughed.

A Castlevania game from a mind like Kamiya’s would definitely be something special. Would it be a 3D action game like Bayonetta, or more of a 2D side-scroller in the vein of Viewtiful Joe ? The possibilities are endless, and given that Konami is already on a mission to revitalize its classic IPs with new games, the possibility of a team-up with CLOVERS on a Castlevania title isn’t totally out of the question.

It's also worth noting that the Castlevania franchise enjoyed a new installment in Belmont's Curse late last month. Alongside its animated adaptations on Netflix, Konami's classic vampire-slaying game series is getting a second wind, and Kamiya would like to be part of that, though whether or not this actually happens remains to be seen.

Kamiya also brought up ideas for other potential games that CLOVERS might make in collaboration with big publishers in the future, though how serious he was about these is up to interpretation. He playfully mentioned making a Star Fox sequel with Koei Tecmo or a King’s Knight sequel with Square Enix, and even mentioned a Kinnikuman M.U.S.C.L.E.: Tag Team Match game with Bandai Namco. Of course, these are all just goofy ideas he likely said in jest, but it does seem like he’s eager to make more games with major companies once Okami is out the door.

The Okami sequel was first announced at the 2024 Game Awards. It’s only been two years since then, so it’s unlikely that we’ll hear anything else from CLOVERS about the game’s development process anytime soon. However, you can read our exclusive interview with Kamiya , done just after the sequel’s TGA announcement, or check out our chat with him from the Lucca Comics & Games Festival just last month.

articles.title: GTA 6 Doesn't Let You Replay Missions, and Rockstar Says There's a Good Reason for That
articles.summary: GTA 6 gives players a lot of freedom in how the story and quests play out, but it came at the cost of letting players replay missions, according to Rockstar.
articles.body:
GTA 6 gives players a lot of freedom in how the story and quests play out, but it came at the cost of letting players replay missions, according to Rockstar.

When speaking with Kotaku , Rockstar Games senior design director Scott Butchard explained why the studio scrapped a mission replay menu in GTA 6. Both GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 allowed players to freely replay missions, but that's not the case in GTA 6 . According to Butchard, they considered bringing the feature back, but cut it because it was "at odds" with the story.

“Mission replay was certainly something we looked at early on in development, and we do not currently support it,” said Butchard. “As the game came together it felt at odds with the story we were trying to tell and felt a bit alien and disconnected. Sitting outside of the game as it were and replaying missions really diminished the choices you had made.”

The lack of a mission replay option has been a point of contention for fans. GTA 6 has some of the best missions in the franchise, particularly the final mission of Chapter 1. Given that GTA 6 can take players anywhere from 50 - 100 hours to finish, most people probably won't start the entire game over just to re-experience their favorite mission. However, it's worth noting that Butchard says the game doesn't "currently support" this feature. Maybe it'll come in the form of an update later, but Rockstar hasn't confirmed that.

GTA 6's story and missions can deviate somewhat significantly based on your choices. Certain characters can be killed or spared, objectives can be completed in different ways, and the entire relationship between Jason and Lucia can vary based on your actions. You can get entirely different dialogue options and cutscenes based on these differences, which might be why a mission replay system isn't as straightforward as it was previous games.

However, Red Dead Redemption 2 also featured different choices that changed Arthur's character. It wasn't quite as nuanced as GTA 6's variations, though. Maybe Rockstar will figure out a way to do this, but it clearly fell low on the priority list, if it was on the list at all by the end of development. Even if Rockstar never adds it, modders will probably find a way to slot it in when the inevitable PC version releases.

articles.title: 'People Are Doing It Too Quickly Now' — The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping Director Speaks Out on YA Franchise Reboots
articles.summary: I got the chance to sit down with the director of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, Francis Lawrence, who opened up about the amount of remakes happening in Hollywood and how he would feel if The Hunger Games series ever got rebooted.
articles.body:
I got the chance to sit down with the director of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, Francis Lawrence, who opened up about the amount of remakes happening in Hollywood and how he would feel if The Hunger Games series ever got rebooted.

Francis Lawrence has directed all but one movie in The Hunger Games series. He’s been with the franchise for over a decade; the first film, directed by Gary Ross, released in 2012, after which Lawrence took up the mantle for all subsequent movies.

It’s one of several iconic movie franchises that defined the YA boom of the 2000s - mid-2010s. And unlike other series from this time period, it has neither languished nor suffered a reboot before its corpse is even cold.

The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes Gallery

HBO’s forthcoming Harry Potter series is perhaps the most egregious example of such a reboot. The last Harry Potter movie released in 2011, and its cast defined an entire generation of fans who grew up watching their adventures at Hogwarts. It seems almost insulting to reimagine the world that was so painstakingly built over the course of a decade — but that’s just my opinion.

I’m not alone in this line of thinking, though. When asked about his feelings on reboots, Lawrence agreed that they’re happening too soon, bringing up Warner Bros.’ thankfully canceled idea for an I Am Legend reboot in 2014, just seven years after the original film was released.

“I mean, I do feel like people are doing it sort of too quickly now,” he mused. “I agree with you on that. People started talking about that with I Am Legend. I don't remember how long ago, but it felt like 10 years had gone by or something, and somebody was thinking of remaking it already at Warner. I'm like, ‘Really? 10 years, that's it?’”

Given the imminent release of HBO’s Harry Potter series on Christmas day, I had to bring up the very real possibility that The Hunger Games sees a reboot in the next decade or so — an idea that Lawrence wasn’t sure would get Suzanne Collins’ blessing.

“I don't know how I would feel about it,” he admitted. “I also don't know if Suzanne has anything in place to sort of protect against that, but that'd be really, really interesting to figure out. But I think it's a tough one. I mean, if Suzanne backed it, I think some spinoffs, and obviously if she writes other books, things like that could be interesting, as long as she backs it and comes up with it and has the thematic reasonings and philosophies that she usually does, that would be cool. But I don't know how you go back and remake the original movies and it not be [Jennifer Lawrence]."

To his point, The Hunger Games franchise has managed to stay in the public consciousness, owing in part to its later release during the YA boom (the final film in the original series came out in 2015) and its two prequel movies that rocked theaters in the 2020s. The latest movie, Sunrise on the Reaping , received solid reviews from critics, earning an 8 out of 10 from IGN.

For more news on this newest entry in The Hunger Games series, check out my interview with star Joseph Zada , who told me all about how he managed to pull off Woody Harrelson's unmistakable accent, and whether or not the cast is Team Peeta or Team Gale .

articles.title: LEGO Announces 4 New Sets Based on the Harry Potter HBO Series
articles.body:
The LEGO Harry Potter theme has been a mainstay since the first set came out in 2001. Now that HBO has a new TV adaptation of the Wizarding World in the works (set to debut on December 25), LEGO has finally unveiled a new batch of sets based on the new series. Four new sets have been announced, two of which are available to preorder now. They're all out January 1. Let’s take a look.

LEGO Harry Potter: Gryffindor Common Room (76482)

LEGO Harry Potter: Hogwarts Express & Platform 9¾ (76487)

LEGO BrickHeadz: Harry, Draco and Hagrid Figures (40992)

The four sets offer a nice selection of characters and locations from the first book, Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone, which is what the HBO show’s first season adapts.

Honestly, these sets don’t look all that distinct from the sets based on the movies. Then again, based on the TV show’s trailer , they didn’t really change much when adapting the franchise into a show.

It all starts on 4 Privet Drive. That’s where we find the home of the Dursley family, who adopt Harry Potter after you-know-who kills his parents. The Dursleys aren’t very nice to Harry, but this LEGO set lets you build their two-story house, complete with Harry’s cupboard under the stairs. This one’s available for preorder now.

LEGO Harry Potter: Gryffindor Common Room

The three main young wizards all end up in house Gryffindor, so they spend a lot of time in the common room. This set recreates that cozy space, complete with a fireplace, five minifigures, and a Quidditch table that’s unique to the show.

LEGO Harry Potter: Hogwarts Express & Platform 9¾

There are so many now-iconic things in the first book that it must have been hard to pick what to base sets on. That said, it would be a shame if there wasn’t a new Hogwarts Express set. This set has platform 9¾, plus the bold red train. It also includes minifigures for Harry, Hermione, Ron, Draco Malfoy, and Molly Weasley — all characters that appear in or around the train in the book.

LEGO BrickHeadz: Harry, Draco and Hagrid Figures

BrickHeadz are kind of like LEGO’s take on Funko Pops. They depict known characters from pop culture, but in a stylized design, and they’re meant for display. These seem like good, blocky renditions of the trio they depict.

articles.title: GTA 6 Animation Director Reveals Rockstar Made 3 Animations for Each Item Interaction
articles.summary: Mike Jones, the director of gameplay animation for GTA 6, revealed that the team at Rockstar created three separate animations for each item interaction in the game.
articles.body:
Mike Jones, the director of gameplay animation for GTA 6, revealed that the team at Rockstar created three separate animations for each item interaction in the game.

If you’ve been playing GTA 6 at all, you’ve probably picked up on the fact that characters can now hold an item in each hand. This has made for some especially funny clips on social media, where users have wasted no time making Jason recreate the ‘six-seven’ meme while holding various objects.

This is a big change from previous Rockstar games; in titles like GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 , players could only carry one thing at a time, though you could dual wield certain guns in GTA: San Andreas. (You could also hold longarms at your side while shooting a pistol in RDR 2 and Max Payne 3 .) Now, you can hold a sandwich in one hand and a drink in the other — or a bag and a gun, if you’re sticking up a pawn shop, for instance. This isn’t just an aesthetic feature, either, as it serves the important function of letting players take care of two tasks at once, making robberies or transporting items a bit smoother.

Players have praised GTA 6 for its jaw-dropping attention to detail, and this particular tidbit wasn’t lost on them. A thread on Bluesky discussing the feature caught the attention of Mike Jones, the director of gameplay on Rockstar’s latest title, who revealed the extent of the studio’s efforts in making sure every single item interaction had a single-handed, two-handed, and hands-free animations.

“FYI, we made three versions for all item interactions; one if both hands are free, one if just your right hand is free and again for the left,” he wrote . “It was a massive pain, but once you knew every interaction could ‘cope,’ it made the game logic much easier. That was then sometimes replicated for crouch, too…”

That being said, the devs at Rockstar aren’t superheroes, and they had to cut corners somewhere during development. Jones admitted this fact in response to another comment in this thread, where a user wrote, “Honestly, the level of polish is so absurd that when I see how cheated the ‘putting gas in the car’ sequence is, I'm like, relieved. ‘Oh, okay, they're human, they bleed.’ You all did SO well.”

“Thanks, everyone would really appreciate your comments! And yes, shortcuts were definitely made, too,” Jones replied.

GTA 6 is a game like no other. Its world is so massive and detailed that some players are avoiding progressing the story in favor of chilling out in Key Lento and diving for treasure, fishing with Cal, and playing billiards at the Rusty Anchor. And we can’t blame them; there’s tons of stuff to do, even in Chapter 1.

articles.title: Rings of Power Showrunner Explains the ‘Different Side’ of Simon Pegg’s Balrog: It ‘Actually Is True to the Books’
articles.summary: The Rings of Power Season 3 is full of creatures and bigger canon references, from Simon Pegg's Balrog to the Fell Beasts, Oliphaunts, Great Eagles and more.
articles.body:
Spoilers follow for The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3, Episodes 1-8.

The third season of Prime Video’s The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power has come to a close, strengthening its ties to author J.R.R. Tolkien's mythology, creatures and iconography, and even explicitly leaning into the design and execution of creatures and places seen in Peter Jackson’s film adaptation. If you’re not a canon expert a la Stephen Colbert, or haven’t re-watched the films recently, below is an explainer on many of the creatures featured in Season 3, with insight into how they connect to the books or the films.

Balrogs were servants of Morgoth, the Dark Lord, during the First Age. After his fall from power, many Balrogs were wiped out in battle, but a few survived. In The Rings of Power narrative, at least one lived deep inside the Misty Mountains, and it was awakened by the dwarves mining for Mithril.

In "Orodruin,” Sauron seeks out that particular Balrog (voiced by Simon Pegg) to gain its knowledge about safely using the Flame of Udûn to forge the One Ring. In return, Sauron promises to free the creature and give it Khazad-dûm to rule. Co-showrunner Patrick McKay told IGN that Tolkien’s text describing the Balrog influenced how they interpreted the fire beast.

“One of the things that's cool in the books is if you really look into the lore that Tolkien built for his entire life, the Balrogs are intelligent super-beings,” McKay explained. “They aren't just monsters. They're cunning and they are battlefield commanders in the First Age. It opened up the possibility that we could show you a different side of him. Maybe one you're not expecting, but one that actually is true to the books and the conception.”

McKay and Episode 7 director Stefan Schwartz described the scene in the Misty Mountains as a dramatic “negotiation” between the Balrog and Sauron. “The scene goes from [Balrog’s] total disdain to actually being won over by Sauron to actually helping him in his quest to create this ring,” Schwartz pointed out.

McKay said casting director Theo Park came up with the idea of asking Simon Pegg to voice the Balrog opposite Charlie Vickers’ Sauron. “Simon Pegg is often known as a comedic actor because of the earliest films he did with Edgar Wright, but he can kind of do anything,” McKay said. “This was an opportunity to do something he hadn't done before, and he took to it like a duck to water.”

Schwartz confirmed that Pegg was on set, performing live into a microphone to Vickers, who was looking at a light box which represented the Balrog’s placement in the frame. “They could rehearse it and run the lines and then actually play it, and then we could talk about the nuance of how he is brought over to Sauron's way of thinking,” he said.

An ally of Sauron’s by the end of Season 3, the Balrog’s rule over King Thrain (Eddie Marsan) and the dwarves will play out in Season 4 (and 5 if it gets a greenlight).

In the opening minutes of Episode 4, "Gundabad," Sauron is introduced to his future steed — an extremely ornery beast that is resistant to the bridle. In Tolkien’s letters, the author described them as winged, stinking creatures with no feathers, just bare skin. The author also referred to them as fell beasts, as well as Nazgûl-birds, which makes sense because in the book version of The Return of the King, fell beasts become the replacement steeds for the Ringwraiths.

However in The Rings of Power, Sauron expounds on their origins more specifically, telling the orcs, “They were once eagles, you know. Until Morgoth blessed them with his touch. Taught them to crave his lash, to survive on only the foulest of meats.” Because of that, Sauron knows the way to tame one is through feeding it living flesh, which he does by feeding it random orcs. The steady meals allow Sauron to bridle the beast, which he first uses to chase Galadriel to Mount Gundabad and then the forests of Greenwood. By the end of the season, Sauron has taught Nazgnagôl Theo ( Tyroe Muhafidin ), and likely the others, how to ride a fell beast. He uses it to dive-bomb the Númenórean army and freak out their soldiers on the eve of battle. Look for them to return when the real war between Sauron and Middle-earth begins in a future season.

The Great Eagle: Saving Our Heroes (Again)

In the last minutes of "Gundabad," before Galadriel, Arondir, Celeborn and Marnûkh are trapped by Sauron and Nazgnagôl Theo on a ledge in Mount Gundabad, Galadriel releases a flaming arrow into the sky like a rescue flare. It spurs a snow-covered Giant Eagle in the mountain to awaken and fly into action. Galadriel instantly recognizes it is Landroval, Prince of Eagles. He gets hit by an orc arrow but survives to save Galadriel and Celeborn from falling to their deaths.

Landroval is a heroic figure across Tolkien’s ages. In The Hobbit, the eagle will save Thorin and company from the burning trees. And at the end of The Return of the King, Landroval is one of the three Great Eagles who rescue Frodo Baggins and Samwise Gamgee from Mordor after they destroy the One Ring.

The elephant-like creatures found south of Mordor are called oliphaunts in Tolkien’s text, and are formally introduced in The Rings of Power in Episode 3, "The Secret Fire.” Gandalf comes upon one in battle armor under the Dark Magic control of Pallando (Ciarán Hinds). Despite getting thrown around by the aggravated beast, Gandalf frees the creature from its constraints in an act of kindness. In "The Lady of Lórien," Gandalf tries to turn Pallando away from Sauron but gets knocked out by the Dark Wizard and is instead bound and strung up to ride prone, on top of an oliphaunt, as he’s taken to Sauron.

In Peter Jackson’s The Two Towers, oliphaunts are visually established in live-action battles, though they are entirely CGI creations. Showrunners Patrick McKay and J. D. Payne decided to carry through that take on the creature into The Rings of Power for continuity.

In Episode 3, "The Secret Fire,” Gandalf has a vision when he visits the Secret Fire and realizes his mission is to redeem Pallando, not conquer him. When he returns to Tom Bombadil’s cottage, his friend is gone and all that’s left is his signature hat. Gandalf takes it as his own, completing the iconic silhouette — long beard, staff and hat — that’s synonymous with the wizard.

In the finale, "The Doom of Men,” Gandalf crosses paths with Tom once again on his long journey back to the elves. His wizarding mentor tells him to keep the hat, cementing its new ownership with his blessing.

What creatures or references did you pick up on in Rings of Power Season 3? Let’s discuss in the comments!

articles.title: Spotify Reveals Massive Spike in Streams for Music Featured in GTA 6
articles.summary: Spotify has released new data that shows huge spikes in streams for music featured in GTA 6, including a Carly Rae Jepsen song from over a decade ago.
articles.body:
Spotify has released new data that shows huge spikes in streams for music featured in GTA 6 , including a Carly Rae Jepsen song from over a decade ago.

In an email sent to IGN, Spotify revealed that the GTA 6 hype is inspiring listeners to add tons of music from the game to their playlists. In addition to hype for the original music created specifically for the game, such as Justice's Flower in a Hurricane, Carly Rae Jepsen's 2015 song Run Away With Me saw a 940% increase in streams following the game's release. The song plays during a pivotal moment in GTA 6's first chapter and is arguably one of the best sections in the game.

Additionally, fans are listening to the official GTA 6 playlist en masse and are actively searching for things related to the game. You can view the full breakdown courtesy of Spotify below.

Following the release of GTA 6, streams of Carly Rae Jepsen's “Run Away With Me” spiked on Nov. 24, increasing by 940% in the U.S. and 1,255% in Canada compared to its average streams.

On Nov. 23, “Flower In A Hurricane” by Justice, Tame Impala, SZA and King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard hit number 1 on BOTH Spotify’s Daily Top Songs charts globally and in the U.S.

Streams of The Official Grand Theft Auto Playlist surged week over week, rising 275% globally and 355% in the U.S. (on Nov. 19 as compared to Nov. 12).

GTA had fans searching for more. Searches containing “GTA,” “GTA6/VI” or “Grand Theft Auto” surged about 510% globally and 600% in the U.S. compared with the week prior (Nov. 19 vs. Nov. 12).

GTA 6 has been shattering all kinds of records and setting new trends. The game had the biggest launch in the history of PlayStation and sold nearly $4 billion worth of copies in its first 24 hours , making it the highest-grossing entertainment launch of all time by a significant margin. The game has also set viewership records on platforms like Twitch , led to a massive increase in internet traffic , and so much more.

It's a massive cultural moment that's likely not going to end anytime soon. Not only will this game likely get bigger, but it also has more big events on the horizon. It's also expected to release on PC early next year, and an online mode is also heavily speculated to come in the future.

Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? Check out the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide right here on IGN. If you're still getting your bearings, discover GTA's new systems with the Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , or get all the details on the first chapters with the Chapter 1 Guide and Tips , Chapter 2 Guide and Tips , and Chapter 3 Guide and Tips . If you're already driving all around Leonida and want to know everything there is to find and do, see the Leonida interactive map .
