In an interview with Eurogamer , Nelson was asked about Rockstar's approach to the systems and themes in GTA 6. He said that a lot of it was born out of all of the work they put into Red Dead Redemption 2, specifically having a reactive world that responds to the player's behavior and choices. He explained that there was a desire to evolve the GTA experience and to "give players choices to interact with the world beyond just violence, beyond just 'down the barrel of a gun.'"

That means players can now point a gun at someone and threaten them, rather than having to beat or kill them to steal their money. The threat of violence is just as prevalent as the violence itself in GTA 6, and it also plays into the morality-adjacent system that is your criminal profile. The game doesn't explicitly punish you for doing bad things, because it's GTA, and you're bound to do bad things. However, it judges you on how harsh you are. If you rob a store with minimal force or only attack people if they draw on you first, attempting to minimize casualties, your profile won't change. If you go in and kill everyone, the level may decrease.

This prompted Rockstar to expand NPC interactions even further. If you drew a gun in GTA 5, no one cared until it was actively pointed at them. Now, people will begin to quietly scurry away if they see you pull a rifle out of your trunk. Nelson explained that while the powerful rampages were fun for a while in previous games, they lacked substance and would get old quickly. In GTA 6, the process to start mowing people down takes a bit more thought because you don't have an endless pocket of weapons anymore.

"You have to call your car," says Nelson. "You have to pop a car trunk and get [a weapon], and now I'm walking, and now people are noticing, but they're sort of sidling away, and it's more believable. And then they're still fleeing in terror, but then there's people who also have guns, and they're shooting at you, or you try to hold somebody up, and they pull a gun, or they grab it, and then you have to deal with them.

"And then, you choose. You're trying to jack somebody off a motorcycle, and they pull a gun on you, and you have to blow their head off, and it's like, 'You shouldn't have made me do that!' And so then it has more meaning, and it's more funny in a way when it's a little bit more pointed. And you can still go on those rampages and basically smash your criminal profile until it breaks, and then you enter this irredeemable state, which basically says, 'I reject your criminal profile system! I don't want it.'"

The more realistic approach with GTA 6 has been a bit divisive for purists. Some don't want consequences; they want a power fantasy, and GTA 6 is decidely not that. If you want a supercar, it's going to take you dozens of hours before you can steal one. There's a progression to the chaos. For some, that's more rewarding. For others who want that quick fix, it's cumbersome. It'll be interesting to see how Rockstar looks at all of the responses to the game and how that informs the next GTA.

Will they go further down this path or will they try to find a greater middle ground? The game certainly isn't hurting despite some vocal critics. GTA 6 is the highest rated game in history on Metacritic and generated nearly $4 billion in revenue in its first 24 hours , making it the biggest entertainment launch in history. IGN gave the game a 10 out of 10 , praising it for its depth and detail.

"Exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered, GTA 6 has not stopped astonishing me since I started it," reads an excerpt from our review. "I regularly find myself in love with video games, but it’s extraordinarily rare that I find myself in complete awe of them. Put simply, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played."

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

Black Friday is almost here, and with it come some of the biggest savings of the year. While there are numerous deals to be found on video games , Blu-rays , and tech , there are also many great deals on clothing available. One of our favorite sales is at Men's Wearhouse, where you can save on suits, dress shirts, shoes, pants, and much more. This is one of the best times of the year to save money on dressier clothes that usually aren't cheap, making these deals a perfect choice for a gift. Below, we've compiled a list of our favorite gifts from Men's Wearhouse this holiday season.

Our Favorite Gift Ideas at Men's Wearhouse This Holiday Season

Men's Wearhouse 2026 Holiday Gift Ideas:

As someone who wears dress shirts daily and sometimes suits, I'd be happy to receive any of these items as a gift. New clothes can get expensive fast, and you can find endless options at Men's Wearhouse right now that will instantly make the MVP of Christmas morning. There are some notable brands available to choose from, including Tommy Hilfiger, Calvin Klein, Kenneth Cole, Joseph Abboud, Michael Kors, and more.

Men's Wearhouse has an excellent selection of dress shirts that fit right in the range of being not cheap, but not too expensive. Even on a short budget, you can likely pick up a pair of dress shirts for under $100, possibly three. There's a good variety of fits and styles available, with straight, classic, slim, and more fits available. You can choose from typical colors like blue or white, as well as patterned options, too.

Alongside dress shirts, Men's Wearhouse also has a great selection of casual shirts that can make a great gift. Styles include standard crewneck tees, polos, button-ups, quarter-zips, and more. These can be a great way to shake up the wardrobe, as often, you can layer these pieces together to make entirely new outfits. I found quite a few casual polos on sale, too, so I recommend looking here if you want to find a gift on the cheaper side.

If there is one category of items that Men's Wearhouse is best known for, it's suits. There are so many options to choose from, with prices ranging from just $150 to over $500 for a two piece suit. You may be surprised by just how many colors and materials there are to choose from. Of course, if a full suit is not what you are looking for, a sport coat is a great alternative. A patterned sport coat can make a great gift, and you can't go wrong with a simple solid either.

Another fantastic route you could go down is buying some pants as a gift this holiday season. Even just one extra pair of dress pants can save you from having to mad dash to the dry cleaners, making this a great choice for any professional. I like the selection at Men's Wearhouse quite a bit, as there are regular dress pants, chinos, five-pocket pants, golf pants, and even shorts.

Depending on the office, chinos and golf pants may be the go-to for daily work. Men's Wearhouse has PGA Tour brand golf pants and shorts available, and these are really comfortable overall. You can easily pull them off for a day in the office, golfing, or even dinner. They're versatile, and the same goes for chinos.

You can find even more gift ideas for the holiday season at Men's Wearhouse, including savings on shoes, sweaters, outerwear, and accesorries.

articles.title: Save Big on Viture’s XR Glasses for Black Friday
articles.summary: One of the best extended reality glasses out there.
articles.body:
Searching for a new display to take your gaming to the next level? XR glasses have a lot of potential, packing what looks like a massive display into a compact pair of glasses you can take with you almost anywhere. For Black Friday , Viture has some of its lowest prices ever with discounts on its Luma series of glasses and even its new flagship Viture Beast glasses, which earned a “Great” rating in our review.

VITURE x 8BitDo Ultimate Mobile Gaming Controller

VITURE USB-C to Glasses and Charging Adapter

VITURE USB-C to XR Glasses & Charging Adapter

The Viture Beast landed this year at $549, but they’re on sale for $489 through Cyber Monday. Our reviewer, Jacqualine Thomas, said in her review, “the Viture Beast XR glasses are a great way to kick back on a flight and play games on a handheld without having to hold up a bulky device the entire way.”

These are the flagship glasses from the brand, offering some substantial tech inside. The Virture Beast pack in a pair of 1200p Micro-OLED displays that run at 120Hz. If that sounds like a brilliant recipe for gaming to you, you’ve clearly been doing your homework on display technology. The OLED displays give you rich contrast — especially with the 1,250-nit peak brightness — vivid color, and fast pixel response times on top of the fluid visual you already get from that refresh rate. The extra brightness of the displays can help if you’re using the glasses out in the daylight, but if you want to maximize the clarity, Viture uses electrochromic dimming that can cut down on external light.

The Viture Beast supports a lot of different use cases, working with phones, computers, and gaming handhelds alike. With adapters, they can work with consoles as well. You can set them up to run as a heads-up display always front and center or even virtually pin the display in space as if it were a monitor mounted in the real world.

Beyond the Beast, Viture has some of its biggest discounts available on the Luma series, which includes the Luma Pro at $339 , Luma Ultra at $449 , and standard Luma at $299 . These still offer capable 120Hz Micro-OLED displays at 1200p and brightnesses from 1,000-1,250 nits. They also all include electrochromatic dimming to let you see through them or darken your surroundings in a snap. If you wear glasses, this series is probably for you, since they include hardware focus adjustments to adapt for myopia.

The Luma is the simplest, offering a 50-degree field of view and sticking to the basics as a display. The Luma Pro stretches the field-of-view slightly, adds in some stylish lighting effects, and adds in a camera for extra spatial capabilities. The Luma Ultra goes yet another step further, upgrading to brighter panel and bringing even more cameras for additional spatial capabilities and hand tracking.

In addition to the savings on the Beast and Luma series, Viture is offering a free 8BitDo Ultimate 2C controller with the purchase of its glasses. It’s also discounting the Pro Mobile Dock to $99 , which gives the glasses extra battery, connectivity options, and can connect to HDMI sources. If you get the Pro Mobile Dock, you can also get a special mount for the Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 for free.

You can find the Viture Beast, Luma series, and more accessories on sale on Amazon , Best Buy , and Viture’s website with these offers running through Cyber Monday .
